basic
demo application, a dummy
app which we'll use to dive into those
essential features.

a Node.js Express
application. So an application that uses the

And
you might be wondering, why is that the
case? Isn't this course about Angular?
Well, yes, it is,
but HTMX is a library that aims to simplify
the process of sending
AJAX requests mostly.
So that aims to simplify the process of
sending behind-the-scenes requests from
inside a website
and of handling the responses to those
requests.
So therefore, in order to
use HTMX and in order for me to show you the
core features that make up HTMX,
we need a backend server. We need a server
to which those requests can be sent, and
that will be this Node.js Express server.
Now, I also use this server to then render
the page which we'll see on the screen and
where we'll use HTMX though.
Because whilst that could be a decoupled web
application, a decoupled frontend,
it's quite common when working with HTMX
to use it in the context of a full-stack
application where you as a developer work on
both the backend and the frontend and where
HTMX is used on pages that are rendered by
the backend. Because as you'll also see
throughout this section and this course,
those requests which HTMX will send to the
backend
actually require responses that send back
HTML code. So you'll need to make sure that
your backend does that anyways, and that's
why it is quite common to have one
integrated application.
And that is exactly what we have here in
this starting project. It's a very simple
Node.js application which offers a GET route
to which we can send requests where I send
back a document,
a document where I have some dummy content.

more to this app. And most importantly,
we'll add a lot of HTMX code to this app
throughout this section.
Now, what's worth noting is that here in
this example project, and actually in all
the example projects I'll
give you throughout this course,
I put this HTML code
into a string and I'm sending back that
string which contains the HTML code as a
response from that server to the frontend.
Of course, in
bigger Node.js projects, you might instead
use a template engine like EJS or
Handlebars.
And I just wanna emphasize that you would of
course use HTMX in exactly the same way as
you'll learn it in this course if you were
using such a setup.
I just use this string-based solution so
that all the code is essentially in one
place and we don't have to deal with a lot

Some HTML code, some HTML document, you
could say,
is sent back from the server to the client,
to the browser therefore.

Now, in order to use this attached project,
you should therefore download it and then
run npm install to make sure that all the
dependencies that are required are
installed.
And then you can start this Node.js server
by running npm start.
And this will start in watch mode so that
whenever you make changes to the Node.js
code and you save them and you then reload
the page,
those changes are reflected instantly

and running as long as you are working on
